title: Completing a 24-hour fluid balance chart: total input and total output
blurb: Total every input and output column on a 24-hour chart and calculate the balance without dropping an entry.
question: A person's 24-hour chart shows oral drinks, an IV infusion at 100 mL/hour, urine and one vomit. What are the total input, total output and balance?

teach.body: Formal rule: total input = every fluid that entered the body (oral, IV, enteral feeds, flushes); total output = every measured loss (urine, vomit, drains, NG aspirate, measured stool or blood loss); balance = total input − total output. Plain English: add up what went in, add up what came out, take one from the other. On every Pearson practice paper, the last item (15) asks for exactly this from a 24-hour chart.

teach.h: Which column does it go in?

rows.label: IV fluids (each hour at the rate)
NG or PEG feeds and water flushes

teach.note: Weighed nappies: the stem tells you to treat 1 g as 1 mL.

teach.caption: 0900 to 1400 inclusive is six hourly entries of 100 mL.

teach.h: Worked example: Daniel on a surgical ward
teach.body: Daniel Brooks, 67, is on a 24-hour chart after a bowel operation. Oral = 200 + 150 + 250 + 100 = 700 mL. IV = 100 mL/hour × 6 hourly entries = 600 mL. Total input = 1300 mL. Urine = 300 + 250 + 350 + 200 = 1100 mL; vomit 120 mL; total output = 1220 mL. Balance = 1300 − 1220 = +80 mL. Sense-check: input is a little more than output, so a small positive number fits.

teach.text: The classic chart errors: leaving out the small output columns (vomit, drain, aspirate), counting one IV hour too few, and typing the balance without its sign. Tick off each entry as you add it, and always finish with + or - and mL.

teach.body: A bag recorded only when complete counts once, as its full volume at that time. Weighed nappies use the stem's rule (1 g = 1 mL). A rate change starts a new IV block: count hours at the first rate, then hours at the second. Totals in mL are typed with no thousands comma: 2150 mL, not 2,150 mL.

items: Input: oral, IV (rate × hourly entries), feeds, flushes.
Output: urine, vomit, drains, aspirate, measured losses.
Count inclusive IV hours: 0900 to 1400 is 6 entries.
Type the balance with its sign and unit: +80 mL, -150 mL.

summary: You can now sort every chart entry into input or output, total each column (including hourly IV entries) and calculate the balance. You can also type it with its sign and unit as Pearson expects.

A.q: A person's 24-hour fluid balance chart shows the following. Oral: 0700 250 mL, 1000 200 mL, 1300 150 mL, 1700 300 mL, 2000 100 mL. Urine: 0600 350 mL, 1200 300 mL, 1800 400 mL. Vomit: 1500 100 mL. What is the total output?
A.why: Urine = 350 + 300 + 400 = 1050 mL. Vomit = 100 mL. Total output = 1150 mL.

whyNot.0: Counted the urine but left out the vomit.
whyNot.1: Added the oral intake to the output; oral fluid is input.

A.q: Ahmed, 70, is on a medical ward. His 24-hour fluid balance chart shows the following. Oral: 0800 150 mL, 1200 200 mL, 1600 200 mL, 2000 150 mL. Intravenous: 0.9% sodium chloride at 100 mL/hour, entered at 0900, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1400, 1500 (7 hourly entries). What is his total input?
A.why: Oral = 700 mL. IV = 100 × 7 = 700 mL. Total input = 1400 mL.

whyNot.1: Counted 6 IV hours; there are 7 hourly entries.
whyNot.2: Counted the IV once (100 mL) instead of once per hour.
whyNot.3: Counted 8 IV hours; there are 7 hourly entries.

A.q: A person's 24-hour fluid balance chart shows the following. Oral: 0700 300 mL, 1000 250 mL, 1300 300 mL, 1700 350 mL, 2100 250 mL. Urine: 0600 400 mL, 1100 350 mL, 1600 450 mL, 2200 400 mL. Wound drain: 0900 70 mL, 2100 50 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.0: Subtracted input from output, which flips the sign.
whyNot.1: Left the wound drain out of the output.
whyNot.2: Right size but no sign; the balance must show + or -.

B.q: A woman on an acute mental health ward is drinking little and is on a fluid balance chart. Over 24 hours it shows: Oral: 0800 100 mL, 1000 150 mL, 1300 200 mL, 1600 100 mL, 1900 150 mL, 2200 100 mL. Urine: 0700 250 mL, 1200 200 mL, 1700 250 mL, 2300 200 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.
B.why: Input = 800 mL. Output = 900 mL. Balance = 800 − 900 = -100 mL (a loss).

whyNot.0: Subtracted input from output, so the sign is wrong.

B.q: A child weighing 14 kg is on a 24-hour fluid balance chart. Wet nappies are weighed (1 g = 1 mL). Oral rehydration solution: 0800 60 mL, 1000 80 mL, 1200 60 mL, 1500 100 mL, 1800 80 mL. Intravenous: 0.9% sodium chloride with 5% glucose at 40 mL/hour, entered at 0100, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0500, 0600 (6 hourly entries). Nappies: 0700 85 g, 1100 70 g, 1600 95 g, 2100 60 g. Vomit: 0900 45 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.
B.why: Input = 380 + 40 × 6 = 620 mL. Output = 310 + 45 = 355 mL. Balance = +265 mL.

whyNot.1: Output − input: the sign is reversed.
whyNot.2: Left the vomit out of the output.

B.q: A client with a learning disability in supported living is on a 24-hour fluid balance chart after a urine infection. Drinks: 0730 200 mL, 1030 150 mL, 1230 250 mL, 1530 200 mL, 1830 150 mL, 2100 100 mL. Urine: 0700 300 mL, 1100 250 mL, 1500 300 mL, 2000 350 mL. What is the total input?

whyNot.0: Added the urine to the input.

C.q: Grace has had a caesarean birth and is on a 24-hour fluid balance chart. Intravenous: Hartmann's solution at 125 mL/hour, entered at 0100, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0500, 0600, 0700, 0800 (8 hourly entries); then Hartmann's solution at 75 mL/hour, entered at 0900, 1000, 1100, 1200 (4 hourly entries). Oral: 1300 200 mL, 1600 250 mL, 2000 200 mL. Catheter urine: 0400 300 mL, 0800 350 mL, 1200 250 mL, 1600 300 mL, 2000 250 mL, 2400 300 mL. Vomit: 0300 150 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.
C.why: IV = 125 × 8 + 75 × 4 = 1300 mL; oral = 650 mL; input = 1950 mL. Output = 1750 + 150 = 1900 mL. Balance = +50 mL.

whyNot.2: Left the vomit out of the output.
whyNot.3: Counted 3 hours at 75 mL/hour instead of 4.

C.q: Mr Patel is nil by mouth apart from sips after surgery. His 24-hour chart shows: Intravenous: 0.9% sodium chloride at 125 mL/hour, entered at 0100, 0200, 0300, 0400, 0500, 0600, 0700, 0800, 0900, 1000, 1100, 1200 (12 hourly entries); then 0.9% sodium chloride at 100 mL/hour, entered at 1300, 1400, 1500, 1600, 1700, 1800, 1900, 2000, 2100, 2200, 2300, 2400 (12 hourly entries). Oral sips: 0900 30 mL, 1500 50 mL, 2100 50 mL. Urine: 0600 400 mL, 1200 450 mL, 1800 500 mL, 2400 450 mL. NG aspirate: 0800 150 mL, 1400 200 mL, 2000 120 mL. Wound drain: 0600 80 mL, 1800 60 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.1: Left the wound drain out of the output.
whyNot.2: Left the NG aspirate out of the output.

C.q: A woman in labour is on a fluid balance chart. Oral: 0600 100 mL, 0900 150 mL, 1200 100 mL. Intravenous: Hartmann's solution at 125 mL/hour, entered at 0700, 0800, 0900, 1000, 1100, 1200, 1300, 1400 (8 hourly entries). Urine: 0800 200 mL, 1100 150 mL, 1400 250 mL. Vomit: 1000 200 mL. Measured blood loss at birth: 1500 450 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.

whyNot.1: Left the measured blood loss out of the output.

reteach.title: Two totals, then one subtraction
reteach.question: Oral 900 mL, IV 600 mL; urine 1200 mL, vomit 150 mL. What is the balance?

blocks.body: Input = 900 + 600 = 1500 mL. Output = 1200 + 150 = 1350 mL. Balance = 1500 − 1350 = +150 mL. Sorting each entry into the right column first stops the commonest errors.

blocks.text: A forgotten vomit or drain entry makes the balance look better than it is. Count the entries in each column before adding.

explain.body: Input includes oral fluid, IV fluid and enteral feeds such as NG or PEG feeds.

test.q: A person's 24-hour chart shows oral fluid 450 mL, NG feed 600 mL, intravenous fluid 500 mL and urine 1200 mL. What is the total input?

whyNot.0: Added the urine, which is output.

explain.body: Output includes urine plus every measured loss: vomit, drain fluid, aspirate.

test.q: A person's 24-hour chart shows urine 1350 mL, vomit 200 mL and drain fluid 150 mL. Total input is 2000 mL. What is the total output?

whyNot.3: Added the input to the output.

explain.body: Balance = input − output. More out than in gives a minus sign.

test.q: A 24-hour chart shows total input 1820 mL and total output 2050 mL. What is the fluid balance? If the balance is a gain, put + before your answer (for example +100 mL). If it is a loss, put - before your answer (for example -100 mL). Please use the correct unit.

explain.body: Each hourly entry at X mL/hour adds X mL. Count the entries, both ends included.
